W Residences Marina View - Singapore unveils branded residential luxury at its sales gallery
article:
On entering the sales gallery for W Residences Marina View - Singapore , visitors encounter a space that departs from the conventional showflat format.

A tunnel-like passage opens into a grand, expansive event space, where a large-scale architectural model of the development takes centre stage.

Opposite the model, a circular bar offers a touch of hospitality during viewings, mirroring the social and lifestyle-oriented experience envisioned for future residents.

Get the latest details on available units and prices for W Residences Marina View - Singapore

The showflats draw inspiration from the cosmopolitan character of Marina Bay. Their designs capture the precinct’s urban setting, vibrant energy and contemporary lifestyle.

These features impressed the panel of judges at the EdgeProp Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026, securing W Residences Marina View - Singapore the Showflat Excellence title.

The accolade recognises projects that effectively convey their design vision to prospective buyers, with assessments based on space utilisation, creativity, originality and practicality.

Sandy Tan, EPEA 2026 judge and founder of interior design firm Chalked, described the project’s show units as “a standout”.

High-end homes with bespoke services

Developed by IOI Properties Group and operated by Marriott International, W Residences Marina View - Singapore is a 51-storey integrated tower that will comprise 683 branded residences set above a five-star W Hotel.

The branded development, which is under construction, will have one- to three-bedroom units ranging from 538 to 1,249 sq ft, as well as four- and five-bedroom units spanning 2,250 to 2,809 sq ft. It will also include three penthouses: a simplex 5,199 sq ft unit and two duplex units measuring 5,350 sq ft each.

Designed to blend five-star hotel services with the comforts of home, the ultra-luxury development pairs bold design with curated lifestyle experiences. Services include round-the-clock concierge assistance and a suite of more than 50 lifestyle and wellness facilities.

The project sits on an 84,148 sq ft site located along Marina View, just a three-minute drive from the sales gallery on Bayfront Avenue.

The public launch of W Residences Marina View - Singapore took place in October last year, with an initial release of 100 units.

This followed a private VVIP preview in July, during which two units were sold: a 1,195 sq ft three-bedder for $3.99 million and an 850 sq ft, premium two-bedroom unit for $2.85 million. Caveats lodged show that the project has sold 15 units as at Oct 26 at an average price of $3,082 psf.

Personalising luxury through design

The sales gallery and all four showflats’ interiors were designed by Hachem Studio. The showflats highlight the one- to three-bedroom and five-bedroom layouts, each tailored to reflect distinct lifestyles and preferences.

Fady Hachem, principal director and founder of Hachem Studio, says the design concept behind the interiors was shaped by the development’s location at Marina Bay, which attracts a “diverse community of successful professionals, entrepreneurs and international homeowners”.

He adds: “Rather than adopting a singular design language across all four residences, we explored different material palettes, colours and furnishings to complement the personalities of the imagined homeowners.”

The three-bedroom show unit, themed “The Motorsport Enthusiast Family”, demonstrates how a home can be tailored to express its occupants’ interests and passions.

At the heart of the design is a hobby room featuring F1-inspired memorabilia, decorative pieces and a car racing simulator, offering potential buyers an interactive way to experience the space.

“For us, luxury is not only about beautiful finishes and furnishings, but also about creating spaces that support individuality, hobbies and meaningful experiences,” Hachem explains.

Where craftsmanship meets creativity

Meanwhile, the five-bedroom show unit is distinguished by its use of spatial planning, refined materials and statement design elements.

Designed for a family that enjoys entertaining, it includes a dedicated cigar and whisky room.

The room incorporates a functional design feature: a large statement artwork that doubles as a sliding partition, which gives the flexibility to either open up or enclose the space.

In the master bedroom, textured glass separates it from the adjoining bathroom, letting light filter through while preserving privacy.

Timber finishes, curated furnishings and contemporary elements lend the showflat a “layer of sophistication”, while ensuring that each space feels “luxurious without being overly formal or predictable”, Hachem notes.

Chalked’s Tan praises the thoughtful use of metal and textured materials, as well as the quality of craftsmanship across the show units.

Another highlight is the distinctive design of the show units. “It is refreshing to see a developer push creativity this far,” she says.

title: Zyon Grand: Integrated development with luxury residences that tick all the boxes
article:
Residences at Zyon Grand , an integrated development along Kim Seng Road in District 3, were an instant hit when they launched. Buyers snapped up 84% of the 706 units available during the launch weekend in October 2025, with prices averaging $3,050 psf.

A year on, Zyon Grand is about 90% taken up. Caveats lodged as at Oct 23 show an average price of $3,066 psf for units sold.

The 99-year leasehold development was crowned the Top Selling Project for the Rest of Central Region (RCR) at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026. The award is based on developers’ sales of new projects over a 12-month period.

Zyon Grand also bagged two other wins at the EPEA 2026: the Sustainability Excellence award for residential mixed-use developments and the People’s Choice award for uncompleted residential projects.

Developed by City Developments Ltd (CDL) and Mitsui Fudosan Group, Zyon Grand features twin 62-storey residential towers, a 36-storey long-stay serviced apartment block and ground-floor retail space.

Attractive location, strong connectivity

Zyon Grand’s major draw is its location, says Sky Seah, academic director at the National University of Singapore and part of the EPEA judging panel.

Though classified as an RCR site, Zyon Grand sits right at the edge of the Core Central Region. The development is a short commute from the CBD and the Orchard Road shopping belt. It also has easy access to lifestyle offerings in nearby neighbourhoods such as Great World, River Valley and Robertson Quay.

The development’s connectivity is another major advantage. Zyon Grand is integrated with Havelock MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line, which is just two stops from Orchard MRT Station, an interchange with the North-South Line. The project is also one stop from Outram Park MRT Station, which is an interchange for the East-West and North-East lines.

Meanwhile, the retail podium, called Zyon Galleria, will offer restaurants, a supermarket and an early-childhood development centre.

Piloting long-stay serviced apartments

Zyon Grand occupies a 164,450 sq ft site that CDL and Mitsui Fudosan purchased through a Government Land Sale (GLS) tender in April 2024.

The partners paid about $1.11 billion, or $1,202 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr), for the 99-year leasehold plot known as Zion Road (Parcel A).

Not long after, Zion Road (Parcel B), a neighbouring plot under the Reserve List of the 1H2024 GLS Programme, was triggered for sale. It was eventually awarded to Allgreen Properties in July 2024 for 730.1million(1,304 psf ppr).

The plot is now the site of the 596-unit Promenade Peak , which launched for sale in August 2025.

Zyon Grand’s site was the first GLS parcel to be sold with a long-stay serviced apartment component, as part of URA’s pilot for its Serviced Apartments II (SA2) housing typology.

SA2 units cater to guests staying for at least three months, compared with the seven-day minimum for standard serviced apartments. Unlike standard serviced apartments, SA2 units do not need to be fully self-contained apartments with kitchen amenities.

‘Neat’ separation

Zyon Grand was designed by Japan’s Nikken Sekkei in collaboration with Singapore’s ADDP Architects.

The pair also partnered on Newport Plaza, CDL’s mixed-use project on the former Fuji Xerox Towers site in the CBD. The 215m, 45-storey development comprises the 246-unit Newport Residences , along with offices, serviced apartments and restaurants.

Newport Residences was also a winner at the EPEA 2026, with judges praising its innovative design that seamlessly incorporates various uses in a single building.

In contrast, Nikken Sekkei and ADDP Architects took a different approach with Zyon Grand.

Here, the firms focused on “making full use of the site’s expansiveness to neatly separate the residences from the serviced apartments”, observes Mark Ong, EPEA 2026 judge and group director at architectural and engineering firm P&T Consultants.

The SA2 block is located at the eastern end of the site. While the entire development has a single main entrance along Kim Seng Road, the residential towers have a separate arrival area from Zyon Galleria and the SA2 block.

The SA2 block also has its own amenities, ensuring the condo facilities are exclusively for residents.

Expressing orchids and ikebana

On completion, Zyon Grand’s twin residential towers will be among the tallest structures in the River Valley-Zion Road area. Standing at 240m, the 62-storey skyscrapers will be a stately addition to the skyline.

They feature a distinctive façade with undulating fins, inspired by the Vanda Miss Joaquim orchid, Singapore’s national flower. Mimicking its petals, the fins add an organic visual element to the buildings.

The slender vertical shapes of all three towers draw from the principles of ikebana, the Japanese art of flower arrangement. Emphasising restraint, balance and harmony with nature, ikebana is often expressed through asymmetry and negative space.

Zyon Grand’s landscaping, helmed by Ecoplan Asia, also pays homage to the national flower, with orchid-shaped planters and water features woven into the design.

More broadly, the landscaping is designed to resemble a tropical rainforest, with multi-tiered green and blue spaces that evoke river valleys and lush terrain.

Premium homes and facilities

Residences at Zyon Grand range from one-bedroom-plus-study apartments of 474 sq ft to five-bedroom supreme apartments of 1,819 sq ft. A five-bedroom penthouse sits at the top of each tower — one measures 2,659 sq ft, while the other spans 2,756 sq ft.

The towers have a north-south orientation. High-floor units facing the southern coastline will have views that include Sentosa, the CBD and Marina Bay.

The project’s interior designer, 2nd Edition, also drew on ikebana principles. The homes have a minimalist design focused on seamless integration, such as large-format wall tiles and sinks that sit flush with countertops to minimise visible joints.

Each home comes with a Haiku ceiling fan; V-Zug and Liebherr appliances; and bathroom fittings from Hansgrohe and Geberit. The kitchens and bathrooms also feature an integrated magnetic accessories wall system with movable shelves.

Extensive lifestyle facilities complement the well-appointed homes. On the main facilities deck on the first floor, these include a clubhouse, multiple pools, a tennis and pickleball court, a yoga studio and a gym.

Sky terraces located on Levels 22 and 43 of both towers offer more facilities, including an outdoor fitness area, a meditation deck and panoramic lookout points.

End-to-end sustainability

Zyon Grand has been awarded the Building and Construction Authority’s Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification, along with badges for Health & Wellbeing, Whole Life Carbon and Maintainability.

The development’s sustainability credentials reflect end-to-end green features that span passive design, efficient systems, deliberate material choices and lower-carbon construction.

Over half of the development is built using prefabricated construction, increasing efficiency and reducing waste. Building materials include those endorsed by the Singapore Green Building Council.

To reduce reliance on air conditioning, design features were chosen to help naturally reduce solar heat gain and promote airflow. These include recessed balconies and ledges that provide shade, porous building and home layouts, and ample green and communal spaces.

Energy-efficient systems back these up. They include high-efficiency air conditioning systems, LED lighting and occupancy sensors in common areas.

River Valley transformation

Zyon Grand is part of a wave of new developments that are reshaping the River Valley-Zion Road precinct. In addition to the 596-unit Promenade Peak, two other developments launched in the area over the past year: the 455-unit River Modern in March 2026 and the 524-unit River Green in August 2025.

Like Zyon Grand, all three projects have been well received, with take-up rates currently ranging from around 73% (Promenade Peak) to 95% (River Modern and River Green), based on lodged caveats.

Another GLS site, River Valley (Parcel C), was awarded in June to a joint venture between Sunway MCL and CSC Land Group at $1,730 psf ppr. The partners are expected to launch a residential development with over 500 units across two 36-storey towers.

The new projects are extending the River Valley residential precinct towards Havelock, says EPEA judge Seah. She expects this to “create a dense and more vibrant neighbourhood” that would appeal to both homebuyers and tourists.

In any case, Zyon Grand’s well-rounded appeal has proven to resonate deeply with buyers. “As an integrated development, its direct MRT connectivity, ease of access to amenities, coupled with luxury finishes and facilities, helped strengthen its overall appeal to investors and owner-occupiers,” Seah says.

title: Meta gets record €53 bil of orders for debut euro bonds
article:
(Nov 4): Meta Platforms Inc has pulled in €53 billion (US$59.7 billion or $76.3 billion) of investor demand for its debut euro bond sale, setting a record for any corporate deal in Europe after offering generous yields to shore up funding for massive investments in artificial intelligence.

Orders for the deal are on track to surpass the more than €31 billion in demand Anheuser-Busch InBev NV received for a 2016 bond sale, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

The Facebook parent is looking to raise as much as €9 billion from investors after selling dollar bonds on Tuesday. Its euro offering comes after one of the busiest-ever stretches for Big Tech debt, with Meta, Microsoft Corp, Oracle Corp and Alphabet Inc tapping markets for almost US$57 billion combined since late last week.

Meta is offering the euro debt in six parts with maturities ranging from just over four years to over 38 years, according to a person familiar with the matter. Final pricing levels for the deal are wider across all tranches compared with those of other hyperscalers that have also issued euro-denominated debt.

“It feels like aeons since Meta’s September outreach to euro investors, and they’ve blessed us with their munificence,” said Matthew Rees, head of global unconstrained fixed income at Legal & General Investment Management.

Concerns about the speed of the debt buildup among hyperscalers and broader questions over whether AI spending will pay off have been pushing the cost of capital for these firms higher, as investors demand better terms.

See also: Grab raises sales, earnings forecasts on rising ride demand

Meta is set to price its 6.26-year tranche at 140 basis points over mid-swaps, while Alphabet priced a six-year bond Monday at 90 basis points.

The difference is even greater at the long end of the curve, with Meta’s 18-year tranche paying a spread of 268 basis points, compared with 185 basis points on the 19-year tranche of Alphabet’s deal this week.

“Levels are very cheap for the rating and hence hard to not get involved, but at the same time we remain cautious given next year’s funding requirements,” said Alex Temple, global fixed income portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments.

See also: State Street CEO says it’s ‘hard to see’ AI as a bubble yet

These levels indicate yields that are more in line with those for bonds rated several steps below Meta’s double-A grade, based on Bloomberg News calculations. This is not a unique situation to Meta, as bond traders place hyperscalers as a group alongside lower-rated borrowers.

Existing euro-denominated bonds from Alphabet and Amazon.com Inc trade well wide of their double-A ratings on the secondary market, based on data compiled by Bloomberg. In some of the longer maturities, they are even wider than for the lower-rated single-A band — reflecting investor unease about future financing needs.

Even so, the lower rates Meta and its peers locked in earlier this year give them additional headroom to absorb higher costs now.

“If you look at blended cost of funding for these companies with all their old low-coupon bonds, they can afford to pay up to get issuance away,” said Al Cattermole, fixed income portfolio manager at Mirabaud Asset Management.

It is Meta’s first bond sale outside its home market. Investors placed as much as US$58 billion of bids for the dollar transaction on Tuesday. Citigroup Inc and Morgan Stanley are managing the euro bond transaction, which is expected to price later on Wednesday.

Technology borrowers who took a three-month hiatus from the US high-grade debt market are returning just as investors grow warier of their spending on the data centres, chips and other infrastructure needed to power AI. Microsoft broke the drought with a US$25 billion sale last week, followed by a US$10 billion deal by Oracle.

The flood of deals arrives as the AI buildout faces greater scrutiny from both investors and politicians. There are also questions over whether Democrats who just swept to control of Congress in the US midterm elections will be as friendly to Big Tech. Voter anger over the vast data centres being built across the country was a major election issue in states like Ohio, where Republican Senator Jon Husted was defeated.

Spreads between AI and non-AI names in the US investment-grade market have diverged in recent months, according to calculations by LPL Financial.

The average cost of debt for tech giants has been increasing with almost every new dollar issue in the past two years. And rising government bond yields driven by lofty energy prices has been another pain point for the sector.

Hyperscaler supply is “more as a sector-specific technical challenge than a broader deterioration in credit fundamentals,” Adam Whiteley, head of global credit at Insight Investment, said in emailed comments.

title: US trade deficit narrows slightly on pickup in goods exports
article:
(Nov 4): The US trade deficit narrowed slightly in September as the value of goods exports rose to a four-month high.

The gap in goods and services trade shrank 0.7% from the prior month to US$105 billion ($134 billion), Commerce Department data showed Wednesday. Economists projected a US$107.9 billion shortfall, based on the median estimate in a Bloomberg survey.

The monthly trade figures, which are not adjusted for inflation, have gyrated through US tariffs, a war-driven jump in oil prices, supply-chain disruptions and surging demand for computers, semiconductors and other components needed to build more data centres.

The value of exports rose 1.9%, led by an increase in outbound shipments of capital goods. Imports increased 1.2%, also led by a surge in business equipment.

The value of inbound capital goods — a category that includes computers and accessories, semiconductors and telecommunications equipment — rose US$11.6 billion from a month earlier to a fresh record. US companies are spending heavily on imported technology to ramp up artificial intelligence capacity.

At the same time, imports of industrial supplies, which include oil and petroleum products, fell US$3.7 billion from a month earlier. The US imported fewer barrels of crude oil than a month earlier, according to the report. Exports of industrial supplies decreased US$1 billion.

See also: US job openings jump to four-month high, lay-offs decline

Imports and exports of nonmonetary gold, a category that has been volatile recently, also declined.

On an inflation-adjusted basis, the overall merchandise-trade deficit widened to US$119.5 billion in September, the largest since March 2025.

Exports of services, a category that includes travel, royalties and financial services, ticked up to a fresh record.

See also: Fed officials back more rate hikes, gradual pace of tightening

By country, the US merchandise trade deficit with Canada shrank. Companies on both sides of the border stepped up shipments this summer to get ahead of tariffs after trade talks fell apart. US tariffs of 50% took effect on billions of dollars of Canadian goods on Aug 22; Canada retaliated with levies of its own.

title: Copper follows stock markets higher as democrats sweep congress
article:
(Nov 4): Copper climbed as stock markets turned higher and the dollar dropped after US midterm elections that saw the Democrats sweep Congress.

Benchmark three-month futures pared early losses to bounce back above US$14,000 a tonne in London, tracking a rebound in US equity futures after an initial selloff.

Democrats won control of both chambers in a result that will leave US President Donald Trump far more hemmed in than in the first two years of his second term, when Republican control of Congress left few checks on his power.

Copper has had a volatile year, touching a record high in September before easing in recent weeks, as concerns over spending on artificial intelligence hurt equities and fuelled fears about global growth. The initial rout in stock markets on Wednesday (Nov 4) came as investors questioned whether a Democratic Congress will impede the development of data centres and associated infrastructure.

Following the Democrats’ win, tighter scrutiny of the AI sector will continue to pressure copper despite short-term price swings, said Li Xuezhi, head of research at brokerage Chaos Ternary Futures Co.

See also: Copper, tin fall with base metals on renewed AI stocks selloff

After the US vote, traders will also be focused on Trump’s potential implementation of a tariff on refined-copper imports — a possibility that has drawn vast amounts of metal into the US.

The prospect of tariffs has driven up Comex copper futures over LME prices since Trump came to office, but in recent weeks the spread between the two contracts has narrowed as doubts grow about whether he will push ahead with the levies. The rise in the cost of living, partly associated with his import duties, was a major reason behind voter discontent.

The front-month Comex-LME spread initially traded at negative levels on Wednesday before rebounding to leave Comex trading at a premium of about US$100 a tonne by mid-morning in London.

See also: Copper recovers as easing tech rout, lower oil calm growth fears

Copper was 0.6% higher at US$14,116 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange as of 10.30am local time, after earlier losing as much as 1.5%. Nickel rallied 2%, leading all metals higher on the exchange.
